name: Canaria-Systems-S3-payload-identity-amendment-v1
reason: The original S3 protocol fixed SHA256 of torch.save container bytes. Reconstructing the exact G7 seed-4300 learned compiler reproduced the recorded source test PPL 18.932213342799887 and the S2 aggregate learned-payload checksum 234473.0256500244 exactly, but re-saving identical learned tensors produced different torch.save container bytes. Therefore file-container SHA is not a suitable deterministic identity check for regenerated payloads.

unchanged_conditions.pass_rule: unconstrained full completes and checksum matches; constrained streaming completes and checksum matches; constrained full fails for a memory/allocation condition before 4096 chunks; both constrained modes use exactly the same 64 MiB extra address-space headroom

deterministic_tensor_content_hash_defini: For each block state_dict: iterate keys in sorted order and SHA256-update key UTF-8 + NUL, dtype string + NUL, shape tuple string + NUL, then contiguous CPU tensor raw bytes in C order.
outcome_policy: No constrained S3 outcome was inspected before this amendment was locked. The original file-container-hash implementation is retained as provenance but is superseded only for payload identity verification.
